ios.desc:
**Stop sinking under your to-do list.**

Every ship has a "Plimsoll Line", a mark on its hull that indicates the maximum safe load. If you load cargo past that line, the ship sinks.

*You are no different.* You have a limit to how much mental "cargo" you can carry in a day. Yet, standard to-do lists encourage you to add infinite tasks until you drown in anxiety.

Plimsoll is a calm, visual planner designed to help you respect your capacity.

**WHY IT WORKS**

*Visual Limits:* Watch the water line rise as you add tasks. When it hits the mark, stop.
*Immediate small action:* Tap on the widget to record your mood without having to see the tasks. No guilt. Or open the "Pause and Breathe" screen from the app to recover from stress.
*Integrates with Reminders app:* Keep using Reminders, Plimsoll enhances your existing tasks.
*ADHD Friendly:* No red "overdue" badges. No flashing lights. Just a safe harbor for your thoughts.

**100% FREE. NO PAYWALLS.**
Tired of "free" mental health apps that lock their best features behind expensive monthly subscriptions? Plimsoll is fully unlocked from the moment you download it. There are no ads, no trackers, and no paywalls. If the app helps you navigate your day, there is an optional "Tip Jar" inside where you can buy me a coffee or give me a push to keep development going.

**A NOTE FROM THE DEVELOPER**

I built Plimsoll because standard planners gave me anxiety. I wanted a tool that didn't yell at me, but instead helped me stay afloat. I built this as a solo passion project to help others find that same peace.

If you are tired of productivity apps that make you feel less productive, welcome aboard.

quotes.text:
Couple of scratch-my-itch apps.

1. Plimsoll Line for dealing with anxieties from mountains of Reminder items, by surfacing the stress factors and taking small actions such as quick journalling and a breathing exercise. The new version with Widget should be released within the next week or two. Version 1 is currently in the iOS App Store. (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/calm-to-do-list-tasks-plimsoll/id6751366557
Calm To Do List&Tasks-Plimsoll). Made it to help my wife (and me!) not get so overwhelmed with things she has yet to do but hasn't started. Also to make it easy to write down things weighing heavy on her mind to alleviate the vicious cycle of emotional decay.

2. Yet-unnamed and -unreleased weather app for planning outdoor activities at times of the day when the weather will be most favorable (or least bad). Made it so that I can plan when to go out to the back yard to bring in more fire wood for the stove in my house. The weather has been tough this winter in the Northeastern US so it finally made me work on the app.
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (February 2026)

quotes.text:
Hello HN,

I’m the developer of Plimsoll Line, an iOS app that tries to solve the anxiety I feel when my to-do list gets too long.

I built this to scratch my own itch. I’ve found that most productivity apps optimize for "getting things done," which often just leads to me feeling overwhelmed and guilty about what I haven't done. My wife struggles with this too, so I wanted to build an alternative that prioritizes mental bandwidth over raw output.

THE CONCEPT

The app integrates with Apple Reminders but adds an emotional layer. You assign an "impact" score to tasks (positive or negative). The app visualizes your net emotional load as a water line. That water line hopefully won't reach the "Plimsoll Line", currently the top edge of the app viewport.

If the water gets too high (too much negative load), the app implies (I need to make the app suggest instead) adding positive tasks or taking steps to reduce the negative impact rather than just grinding through the list.

It’s designed to stop you from overloading your "ship" before it sinks (it won't, at least not in the app).

TECHNICAL / PRIVACY

* Stack: Native Swift/SwiftUI.

* Integration: It reads/writes directly to the built-in Reminders database (EventKit). This means you can keep using the default Reminders app and Siri alongside this.

* Privacy: The reminders and emotional impact data are 100% local. No accounts. There is device ID that gets saved on a backend server that tracks whether you've made an in-app purchase …
